entry.summary: A visitor visa for up to 30 days on arrival.
entry.pre_arrival: Online Palau Entry Form up to 72 hours before arrival (free; beware of scams). Declare medicines on it. An onward or return ticket.

tourism.detail: The visa is for tourism, leisure and social visits, not work. It can be extended twice for 30 days. The USD 100 Pristine Paradise Environmental Fee is normally included in the international air ticket.
tourism.next: Submit the entry form within the 72-hour window, carry onward travel and funds, and sign the Palau Pledge on arrival.

meetings.detail: The official immigration page lists business meetings, conferences, contract negotiation and opportunity exploration. It does not permit employment or commercial operation.
meetings.next: Carry an invitation and keep the visit to discussion, negotiation and exploration unless a labour permit is approved.

conference.route: Tourist or business visa for attendance
conference.detail: Palau includes meeting and conference attendance in short visitor purposes. A diplomatic or leaders' meeting can impose separate accreditation and security requirements.
conference.next: Confirm organiser accreditation and whether the role is passive attendance or active program delivery.

unpaid-speaking.route: Direct Immigration and Bureau of Labour classification before travel
unpaid-speaking.detail: Palau publishes no general visitor exemption for an unpaid keynote, reading, workshop or panel. Its visitor pages prohibit employment and commercial activity and require a labour permit for work, so no-fee status should not be treated as decisive.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the Palauan host send the complete role, expense support and schedule to Immigration and Labour and retain the written answer or permit.

paid-speaking.route: Labour permit and locally compliant contract
paid-speaking.detail: Paid speaking, consulting or facilitation is outside the visitor lane. The host must resolve the labour permit, business licence and tax treatment before delivery. Palau's tax legislation can apply 10% non-resident tax to a technical fee, while a continuing business presence can move into business-profits rules.
paid-speaking.next: Contract only after the host obtains the labour permit and written Bureau of Revenue and Taxation classification for the fee.

book-launch.route: Labour classification plus local publisher or bookseller and customs plan
book-launch.detail: Publisher meetings can remain business visits. A reading, promotion, signing service, imported stock or local sale can become work or commercial activity and should be handled by a Palauan counterparty.
book-launch.next: Use a local bookseller, library, school or cultural host to clear the appearance, imports, sales and community protocol.

ai-teaching.route: Host-backed labour permit or written exemption
ai-teaching.detail: A community, college, government or organisational AI workshop is active teaching or professional delivery. No published short-teacher visitor exception was found.
ai-teaching.next: Have Palau Community College, government, school, NGO or other host seek Immigration and Labour clearance before fixing dates.

remote-work.route: No published physical digital-nomad work permission
remote-work.detail: Digital Residents can seek two consecutive 90-day tourist-visa extensions after the initial visa, but the official page does not convert that tourist stay into permission to work. Palau digital residency should not be confused with physical work rights.
remote-work.next: Do not use a Digital Resident ID as work permission; obtain written Immigration and Labour advice or a labour and residence route for the actual activity.

entrepreneur.route: Foreign Investment Approval Certificate, entity, business licence, tax registration and labour permit
entrepreneur.detail: A non-citizen investor should establish the company structure, apply to the Foreign Investment Board for an FIAC and then complete business, tax and work permissions. The Foreign Investment Act gives the Board up to 90 days after a complete application and applies community-benefit, citizen-participation and compliance considerations.
entrepreneur.next: Use the first visit for discovery, then complete the FIAC checklist, company charter, business licence, PGST and labour sequence before operation.

trade.route: Business visa for negotiation; FIAC, licence and labour permission for operations
trade.detail: Contract negotiation and opportunity exploration fit the business visit. Importing for sale, local retail, installation or service delivery becomes commercial activity and needs a Palauan entity or licensed local partner, customs and work permission.
trade.next: Appoint a Palauan importer or distributor and separate samples, temporary professional equipment, stock for sale and after-sales service.

artist.route: Labour permit or written exemption plus Palauan cultural and venue approval
artist.detail: Performance, filming, exhibition and cultural collaboration should be cleared with the local host, state and traditional leadership where relevant. A small-community invitation does not automatically waive labour, tax or merchandise rules.
artist.next: Co-design the activity with a Palauan cultural host and obtain written labour, venue, state, community and tax clearances before publicity.

mixed-mission.route: Business visitor entry for exploration plus labour, FIAC and local approvals for active work
mixed-mission.detail: Meetings, Forum-related observation, AI teaching, community work, books, art and business development can share a visit, but Palau's visitor lane stops at work and commercial activity.
mixed-mission.next: Give one local coordinator a simple ledger of every activity, payer, customer, state, community and item entering Palau, then obtain written clearance line by line.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are strict. Long sentences apply for possessing illegal 'hard drugs'. Hard drugs include heroin, cocaine and synthetics.
laws.heading: Drug laws

laws.rule: A traditional bul (decree by traditional leadership) is in effect in Koror and Airai. This decree is a curfew in place between midnight and 5am in the hamlets (suburbs) to reduce petty crime related to drug use. A similar measure is in effect in the states of Ngarchelong and Ngiwal. Foreigners are unlikely to be the target of these measures and application is inconsistent. However, it is still recommended that you follow the advice of local authorities and have a genuine reason to be in these areas during these times. The legal drinking age is 21 years. laws.rule: Dress and behaviour standards are conservative.
laws.heading: Dress standards

laws.rule: Same-sex relationships are legal, but cultural attitudes can be conservative. Avoid public displays of affection.

laws.rule: You are required to declare medications on your Palau Entry Form.

laws.rule: To drive in Palau for up to 30 days, you may need: an International Driving Permit (IDP) a valid Australian driver's licence You must get your IDP before you arrive. After 30 days, you must get a local licence.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the US Dollar (USD). ATMs are available in larger centres and at the airport. Most shops in Palau accept credit cards. Some shops will only accept cash. Check with the shop in advance or have both payment options available.
